page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Threshold stimulus
steps.why: A sub-threshold stimulus produces only a small local change in the membrane potential that fades without spreading, so no action potential forms; at or above the threshold the impulse formed is always full size, whatever the strength of the stimulus.
common_mistakes: Writing that a bigger stimulus gives a bigger impulse. It does not.
steps.memory_tip: Below the threshold no impulse forms; at or above it, the full impulse forms.
lines: An action potential occurs in response to
but not to a sub-threshold stimulus.

steps.label: It goes all the way
steps.why: Once started, the impulse regenerates itself along the fibre, so it cannot fade out half way.
common_mistakes: Saying the impulse weakens along the fibre. It does not.
Leaving out the conclusion that gives the principle its name.
steps.memory_tip: Either the whole impulse or none of it.
lines: Once generated it cannot be stopped part
way. It travels completely to its

lines.text: So it is called the all-or-none principle

insider_note: Two things are marked: the threshold or above-threshold stimulus in the first line, and that once started the impulse travels completely. Write both, then name the principle.
